profile: Actual native application, local Codex generation, real Tavily/cache; not deployment-provider evaluation
method: Fresh questions stay undisclosed through the next runtime freeze and six one-shot application captures. Independent review uses captured citations and source text only, with no new external searches. Scores from the first eighteen remain unchanged.

rubric.scale: Each dimension is scored 0, 1, or 2: absent or materially wrong; partially useful; fully supported and useful. Every requested output must be tracked separately.

dimensions.request_coverage: Addresses every requested part; an explicit evidence gap counts as honest handling but not as a substantive answer. Does not mark a silently omitted part complete.
dimensions.useful_synthesis: Answers in plain language, prioritizes material findings, explains their relevance, and distinguishes evidence from interpretation. Avoids a string of source metadata and repeated caveats.
dimensions.provenance: Material factual claims have inspectable supporting citations. Filing facts, calculations, issuer statements, and third-party views remain distinguishable; duplicate views of one source do not imply corroboration.
dimensions.honest_limits: Does not invent dates, completed transactions, causation, or public consensus. Timeframes and partial coverage are stated briefly when material. Unsupported scope is identified without discarding supported parts.

failure_conditions: A requested part is omitted while the response is complete.
A material financial or event claim is unsupported, or an unsupported consensus is invented.
Explicit filings-only instructions trigger live research.
An unsupported price request receives an invented quote or blocks an otherwise answerable filing request.
The response consists primarily of restrictions or search diagnostics despite having usable relevant evidence.
rubric.evaluation_note: Do not require particular current events, exact routes, exact phrasing, a fixed number of sources, or a positive news finding. Judge response quality against evidence actually available. A supported no-finding answer can pass when scope and search coverage are clear.

decision_policy: Supported useful answers pass despite minor editorial issues. False evidence gaps, invalid scope rejection and internal-dependency requirements fail usefulness even when substantive surviving claims are supported. Honest partial evidence is not equivalent to fabricated completion.

summary.latency_note: End-to-end native application latency includes server scheduling and any overlap with a queued development-regression request. No deployment-provider/cold-start claim is made.
remaining_defects: calendar year rejected against historical fiscal controls
explicit datelines not normalized and false missing-date status
overbroad paragraph suppression in development regression
summary.budget_note: Global counters include other task activity; not isolated held-out-call consumption.

A sourced explanation of similarities or differences in their approaches
criteria: Covers both companies with a clear recent timeframe
Does not force an unsupported direct performance ranking
Explains significance in readable language and distinguishes plans from realized events
Does not claim missing dated evidence when cited usable dates exist
cases.reason: Both companies receive meaningful updates and a supported comparison. One AMD bullet starts 'At the same event' after the relevant introduction was removed; useful overall but editorially rough.
source_checks: W10 and its preserved search observation support the open full-stack framing, Anthropic engineering/deployment agreement and OpenAI Q4 deployment plan.
W3 explicitly identifies NVIDIA as the source of the syndicated August 31 MediaTek/NVLink Fusion announcement.
W1 supports Cisco's August 25 secure-AI-factory expansion through Supermicro.
Planned deployment is not represented as completed operation.

cases.question: ive seen people saying amds ai business is taking off. what has amd itself actually announced recently, and whats an announcement vs something already in production
required_outputs: A distinction between announced or planned capacity and production or deployment already claimed
criteria: Uses issuer-attributed evidence for the requested official claims
Recovers explicit page publication dates where available instead of requiring a populated API date field
Attributes production claims to AMD rather than pretending independent verification
Keeps caveats proportional and does not retain unsupported factual assertions
cases.reason: Official source text establishes dated announcements and separates production, testing and future deployments, but null normalized date metadata still generates a contradictory no-dated-development gap.
source_checks: W3 explicitly says SAN FRANCISCO, July 23, 2026 and Helios 'now in production'; it separately describes OpenAI's Q4 plan and Meta testing.
W1 explicitly says July 22, 2026 and supports the future Anthropic deployment and up-to-5-billion-dollar investment commitment.

All three normalized published_date fields are null despite explicit datelines in their returned text. The final global no-date gap is false.
